title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-07-16
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD

ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard capture of a classic July‑16 1966 Fillmore show with standout versions of In the Pines, Cream Puff War and Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller‑transferred soundboard tape is praised as crystal‑clear and full‑bodied, delivering an almost “pristine” listening experience despite a few missing intro/outro cuts. Musically the performance shines with early‑Dead energy – Jerry’s Gibson tone, Pigpen’s organ/harmonica and tight group interplay make songs like In the Pines, Cream Puff War and Viola Lee Blues unforgettable. While a handful of tracks suffer from edits or mic issues, the overall vibe is an essential snapshot of the Summer‑of‑Love era.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 stars and praise both performance and audio; only a few low/mixed scores note minor cuts, yielding an average ~4.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller’s transfer is described as crisp, pristine and full‑bodied; the mix balances guitars, organ and vocals beautifully. Minor issues are limited to edited openings/closings and a mic drop on Cardboard Cowboy.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑66 set with folk/blues focus; a label‑show format keeps the pacing tight, though a few edits interrupt continuity. Overall the flow feels historic and engaging.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his Gibson tone, mind‑bending chord work and vocal on Cream Puff War.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as great; his bass tones are described as “cranked‑Marshall‑ish” and solid throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ/harp gets enthusiastic shout‑outs (“shrill”, “surf rockin’ those keys”), highlighting his blues frontman role.
